summary: A post composer and scheduler you run yourself: write threads in a clean editor with correct weighted character counts, queue them into slots, and publish through the X API or, because that API now costs per post, get a notification at slot time and a copy-to-clipboard button that keeps the tool useful without paying X anything.

stack.why: drafts, queue and scheduler loop in one process
the only correct way to count 280 weighted characters

stack.choice: X API v2, optional, behind an interface
stack.why: pay-per-use pricing means the fallback comes first
a reminder at slot time is the free publishing path

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your timezone, written as an IANA name
prerequisites.why: The scheduler stores UTC and renders in your zone. Getting this wrong posts at the wrong hour twice a year.
prerequisites.get: Look it up: Europe/London, America/New_York, Asia/Karachi. Put it in .env as TIMEZONE.

prerequisites.name: Your posting slots
prerequisites.why: Phase 3 fills slots you define, such as weekdays at 09:00 and 16:00.
prerequisites.get: Write them as a JSON file: days and times in your timezone.

prerequisites.name: An ntfy topic (or another notification channel)
prerequisites.why: The free publishing path is a notification at slot time. ntfy needs no account: pick a long random topic name.
prerequisites.get: Install the ntfy app on your phone, subscribe to a topic like posts-<random>, and put the topic in .env. Test with curl -d 'hello' ntfy.sh/<topic>.

prerequisites.name: An X developer account with pay-per-use billing (optional)
prerequisites.why: Only needed for automatic posting. As of 2026 there is no free tier for new developers: roughly $0.015 per post and about $0.20 per post containing a link. A link-heavy habit costs more than Typefully.
prerequisites.get: developer.x.com > sign in > create a project and app > User authentication settings with Read and Write > generate API Key, API Secret, Access Token and Access Token Secret. Add a payment method for pay-per-use. Verify the current prices in the console; they have changed repeatedly.
prerequisites.cost: pay per use, about $0.015 per post, $0.20 with a link

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: TIMEZONE
env.where: IANA zone name. Verify before the first scheduled run.

env.name: MEDIA_DIR
env.where: Attached images, resized and stripped of EXIF.

env.name: NTFY_TOPIC
env.where: The topic you subscribed to in the ntfy app.

env.name: X_API_KEY
env.where: X developer portal, only if you publish automatically.

env.name: X_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.where: X developer portal, generated with Read and Write.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Composer and drafts
phases.goal: Write threads, split them with ---, never lose a word.

steps.do: Create the project and the drafts, posts and revisions tables
steps.detail: drafts (id, title, created_at, updated_at, status), posts (id, draft_id, position, body, media JSON), revisions (id, draft_id, body, saved_at).
commands: mkdir composer && cd composer && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.detail: A distraction-free textarea; --- on its own line splits into post cards rendered beside it. Autosave on a debounce, keeping a small revision history.

steps.do: Add drag to reorder posts within a thread

check: Adding and removing --- splits and re-joins correctly
A browser refresh loses nothing
Reordering persists
A previous revision can be restored

phases.title: Correct character counting

steps.do: Install twitter-text and count with config v3
steps.detail: 280 weighted characters; every URL counts as 23 regardless of length; CJK and emoji count 2. Not string.length.

steps.do: Show the weighted count per post and block queueing an over-limit thread

check: A post with a 100-character URL counts it as 23
An emoji counts as 2
A 280-weighted post is accepted and 281 is refused
Counts match X's own composer on pasted real examples

phases.title: Queue and calendar
phases.goal: Slots from your file, next-free-slot, a calendar by day, no double booking.

steps.do: Create the queue table and load SLOTS_FILE
steps.detail: queue (id, draft_id, scheduled_for UTC ms, attempts, last_error, posted_at, remote_ids JSON). Convert slots from TIMEZONE to UTC when scheduling.

steps.do: Add next free slot, an explicit picker, and a calendar view grouped by day

check: Three drafts into two daily slots spread across two days
Next free slot never returns a past time
A taken slot is not offered again
A slot at 09:00 local shows as 09:00 across a DST change

phases.title: Publishing, fallback first
phases.goal: Useful with no API key at all; automatic posting only when configured, with the cost stated.

steps.detail: A copy-thread button that copies the whole thread formatted for manual posting.

steps.do: Send an ntfy notification at slot time
steps.detail: The scheduler loop, every minute: for each due item with no API key, post to ntfy.sh/NTFY_TOPIC with the first line and a link to the draft.
commands: curl -d 'Time to post: your thread title' ntfy.sh/$NTFY_TOPIC

steps.do: Add the X API publisher behind an interface
steps.detail: OAuth 1.0a user context. Post each item as a reply to the previous one; record remote ids; three retries on transient errors, never on a rejected post.
Count published posts and link posts this month and estimate the bill from the prices you verified.

check: With no key set, a due item fires a notification and the copy button yields the full thread
With a key set, a two-post thread publishes as a real reply chain
A rejected post is marked failed exactly once with the API's error visible
Overdue items after a restart publish or notify on the next loop
traps: Never retry a rejected post. You will publish it four times.
Verify X's prices in the developer console before relying on them; they have changed repeatedly.

phases.title: Media
phases.goal: Up to four images per post, resized and stripped.

steps.do: Attach images per post with sharp: resize, strip EXIF, store in MEDIA_DIR
Enforce four per post and upload media before posting when the API path is on

check: A four-image post publishes or copies correctly
A fifth is refused in the UI
No stored file retains GPS EXIF

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: Live, backed up, queue survives restarts.

steps.do: Add /healthz, systemd, Caddy and a backup of data/

steps.detail: The X cost per post and per link post with the date checked and a link to the console; the sentence that daily link posting costs more than the subscription; the timezone check.

check: A restart leaves the queue intact and nothing due-while-down is lost
The README states the current X prices with a date

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the scheduler is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A scheduler that is honest about what publishing costs, works fully without paying X, and can be extended to other networks behind the same publisher interface.

architecture.swap: Any front end writing the same rows
A cron job calling one function

architecture.owns: the interface with X, ntfy and clipboard implementations
architecture.swap: Add LinkedIn or Bluesky as another implementation
Object storage behind the same functions

operations.backup: tar of data/ nightly off the box.
operations.restore: Extract, start, confirm the calendar shows the queue.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz; alert if a due item is more than 15 minutes late.
operations.incident: If X keys leak, revoke them in the developer portal and rotate. If the API rejects everything, the fallback notifications keep the queue useful while you investigate.

releaseGate: Works end to end with no X key configured
Character counts verified against X's composer on ten examples
One restore drill performed and dated
README states the X costs with a date

notIncluded: LinkedIn and other networks in v1. Each is its own API, auth model and content format.
Analytics on published posts: reads cost money per call under pay-per-use.
Multi-account, teams and AI rewrite suggestions.
after: Bluesky as a second publisher: its API is free and the interface is already there
A browser bookmarklet that opens the composer with a quoted link
